nominative-01.whyEnding: Kot is a masculine noun ending in a consonant. Its singular naming form has no added ending; compare feminine książka with -a and neuter dziecko with -o.

nominative-07.whyEnding: Student is masculine and ends in a consonant. Its nominative singular is the unchanged dictionary form; its plural studenci has a different stem.

nominative-13.whyEnding: Lekarz is masculine and ends in a consonant. Nominative singular keeps the dictionary form without an added ending; compare feminine książka.

genitive-02.whyEnding: Dom is masculine inanimate and has lexical genitive singular -u: domu. Some masculine inanimate nouns instead take -a, such as chleb → chleba; learn the choice with the noun.

genitive-06.whyEnding: Czas is masculine inanimate and has lexical genitive singular -u: czasu. Compare animate kot → kota with -a; masculine nouns do not share one genitive ending.

genitive-11.whyCase: Widzieć normally takes an accusative direct object. Nie negates widzę, so its direct object pies appears in the genitive here.
genitive-11.whyEnding: Pies is masculine animate, whose genitive singular is psa. The movable vowel ie disappears from the stem; compare kot → kota, which keeps its stem.

genitive-13.whyCase: Znać normally takes an accusative direct object. Nie negates znam, so the object miasto is genitive in this sentence.
genitive-13.whyEnding: Miasto is a neuter noun ending in -o. Its genitive singular replaces -o with -a: miasta; compare dziecko → dziecka.

genitive-14.whyEnding: Praca is a feminine noun ending in -a. Its genitive singular has -y after c: pracy; compare szkoła → szkoły and książka → książki.

genitive-15.whyCase: Mieć normally takes an accusative direct object. Nie negates mamy, so chleb is genitive here.
genitive-15.whyEnding: Chleb is masculine inanimate, but its genitive singular is chleba with -a. Masculine inanimate nouns can choose -a or -u lexically; compare dom → domu.

genitive-16.whyEnding: Pomoc is feminine despite ending in a consonant. Its genitive singular is pomocy with -y; do not apply the -a-noun pattern blindly.

dative-01.whyEnding: Masculine kot uses the shorter dative singular -u: kotu. Other masculine nouns use -owi, as in przyjacielowi; the choice is partly lexical.

dative-02.whyEnding: Feminine kobieta takes dative singular -e/-ie with a softened stem: t becomes ci, giving kobiecie. Compare książka → książce with k → c.

dative-06.whyEnding: Masculine personal przyjaciel takes the common dative singular -owi: przyjacielowi. Kot instead has lexical -u: kotu.

dative-07.whyEnding: Masculine brat takes the shorter dative singular -u: bratu. Other masculine nouns use -owi, such as przyjaciel → przyjacielowi.

dative-11.whyEnding: Masculine personal nauczyciel takes common dative singular -owi: nauczycielowi. Kot instead has -u: kotu.

dative-12.whyEnding: Kolega is masculine despite singular -a. In dative singular, g softens to dz before -e, giving koledze.

dative-13.whyEnding: Pies has dative singular psu. The movable ie vowel disappears before -u; compare kot → kotu, which keeps its stem.

dative-14.whyEnding: Ojciec has dative singular ojcu. The stem contracts from ojciec to ojc- before -u; learn this common irregular form.

dative-15.whyEnding: Neuter miasto replaces final -o with -u in dative singular: miastu. Compare dziecko → dziecku.

dative-16.whyEnding: Feminine siostra uses -e in dative singular and the stem r softens to rz: siostrze. Compare książka → książce with k → c.

accusative-02.whyCase: Czytać takes a direct object; książka is what is being read, so the object is accusative.

accusative-03.whyCase: Pić takes a direct object; woda is what is being drunk, so the object is accusative.

accusative-13.whyEnding: Kawa is a feminine -a noun. Its accusative singular replaces -a with -ę: kawę, as in książka → książkę.

instrumental-13.whyEnding: Ołówek is masculine. Its instrumental singular is ołówkiem: the movable e in -ek disappears and -iem follows the k stem.

instrumental-01.whyEnding: Masculine kot takes common instrumental singular -em: kotem. Feminine -a nouns instead often take -ą, as in książką.

instrumental-02.whyEnding: Długopis is masculine; instrumental singular adds common -em: długopisem. Feminine książka instead gives książką.

instrumental-03.whyEnding: Nauczyciel is masculine personal. Its instrumental singular adds -em: nauczycielem; feminine -a nouns commonly take -ą instead.

instrumental-08.whyEnding: Masculine brat takes instrumental singular -em: bratem. Feminine -a nouns commonly use -ą, as in książka → książką.

instrumental-09.whyEnding: Masculine personal student takes instrumental singular -em: studentem. Feminine -a nouns commonly use -ą instead.

instrumental-10.whyEnding: Masculine pociąg takes instrumental singular -iem after g: pociągiem. Compare kot → kotem without the written i.

instrumental-15.whyEnding: Lekarz is masculine and takes instrumental singular -em: lekarzem. Compare feminine książka → książką with -ą.

instrumental-16.whyEnding: Autobus is masculine and takes the common instrumental singular -em: autobusem. Compare feminine książka → książką.

locative-13.whyEnding: Film is masculine; its locative singular adds -ie: filmie. Compare kot → kocie, where the stem also changes.

locative-02.whyEnding: Dom has locative singular domu with lexical -u. Other masculine nouns use -e/-ie, such as kot → kocie; learn this ending with the noun.

locative-05.whyEnding: Neuter dziecko has locative singular dziecku with -u after its k stem. Compare neuter miasto → mieście, which changes stem and takes -e.

locative-06.whyEnding: Neuter krzesło has locative singular krześle. The stem consonant softens (s → ś) before -e; compare dziecko → dziecku with -u.

locative-07.whyEnding: Neuter miasto has locative singular mieście. Both the vowel and the st cluster change in this form, so learn it as a whole; compare dziecko → dziecku.

locative-12.whyEnding: Feminine poczta takes locative singular -e, and t softens to ci: poczcie. Compare książka → książce with k → c.

locative-09.whyEnding: Feminine praca has locative singular pracy with -y after c. Other feminine -a nouns take -e/-ie and may change the stem, as in książka → książce.

locative-10.whyEnding: Masculine park has locative singular parku with -u. Compare kot → kocie with -ie and a softened stem; the singular ending is noun-dependent.

locative-11.whyEnding: Feminine mama replaces final -a with -ie in locative singular: mamie. Compare książka → książce, where k also softens to c.

locative-14.whyEnding: Warszawa is a feminine place name ending in -a. Locative singular replaces -a with -ie: Warszawie.

locative-15.whyEnding: Ławka is feminine. Before locative singular -e, k softens to c: ławce, like książka → książce.

locative-16.whyEnding: Język is masculine; its locative singular is języku with -u. Compare kot → kocie with -ie and a stem change; learn which ending each noun takes.

vocative-13.whyEnding: Brat uses vocative singular -ie with a softened stem: t → ci, giving bracie. Compare kot → kocie with t → c.

vocative-08.whyEnding: Piotr takes vocative singular -e, with r softening to rz: Piotrze. Compare przyjaciel → przyjacielu with -u.

vocative-05.whyEnding: Masculine personal przyjaciel takes vocative singular -u: przyjacielu. Compare kot → kocie with a different ending and softened stem.

vocative-06.whyEnding: Masculine title pan has vocative singular panie with -ie. Compare przyjaciel → przyjacielu with -u; learn common address forms individually.

vocative-07.whyEnding: The familiar feminine name Kasia has vocative singular Kasiu with -u. Many feminine -a nouns instead use -o, as in mama → mamo.

vocative-09.whyEnding: Masculine syn has vocative singular synu with -u. Compare kot → kocie with -ie and a softened stem; the ending varies by noun.

vocative-14.whyEnding: Doktor uses vocative singular -e and r softens to rz: doktorze. Compare przyjaciel → przyjacielu with -u.

vocative-16.whyEnding: Koleżanka is feminine and ends in -a. Its vocative singular replaces -a with -o: koleżanko, like mama → mamo.
